title: Skill-gate onboarding sprint and hiring intake protocol
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Summary:
This protocol defines a unified flow from hiring intake through offer acceptance and a focused 4-week "onboarding sprint" gated by explicit skill-readiness criteria (the "skill-gate"). It reduces time-to-role-readiness, improves hiring quality by aligning hiring managers and interviewers early, and creates objective evidence for manager sign-off at role activation.

Goals:
- Standardize intake so roles are assessed, scoped, and resourced consistently.
- Create a lightweight, repeatable "skill-gate" that clarifies what "ready to operate independently" means for a role.
- Reduce variance in first-90-day outcomes by using a 4-week onboarding sprint with measurable checkpoints.
- Ensure managers, people-ops, and hiring panels share accountability for candidate evaluation and post-offer ramp.

Scope:
Applies to all full-time hires and internal role transfers in engineering, product, and platform teams. Exclusions: interns (follow intern onboarding guide), executive hires (executive hiring playbook).

Owner and contacts:
- Process owner: People Ops (Priya Nambiar) — process updates and intake template maintenance.
- Intake approvers: Hiring manager + Team lead + People Ops intake partner.
- Onboarding sprint owner: Hiring manager (executes sprint), mentor (peer assigned), and People Ops (coordination).
- ATS / HRIS: Greenhouse (ATS), Workday (HRIS). For automation hooks: see integration runbook (related_pages).

Quick definitions:
- Intake: the initial form that defines role purpose, success metrics, and the skill-gate checklist.
- Skill-gate: the minimal set of technical and behavioral capabilities required to be considered "independently contributing" in the role after onboarding sprint.
- Onboarding sprint: a structured 4-week plan with day-by-day and week-by-week milestones with manager and mentor checkpoints.

1) Hiring intake process (timeline: 1–3 business days)
1. Hiring manager submits Intake form (Greenhouse intake linked) — required fields: role summary, top 3 success metrics (first 6 months), mandatory & desired skills, headcount justification, expected TSR (Total Salary Range), interview panel nominations, preferred start window.
2. People Ops partner reviews within 24 hours: checks comp band, headcount, remote/office eligibility, and necessary approvals.
3. Hiring manager + people ops + team lead align on skill-gate and interview rubric in a 30-minute intake sync (scheduled within 3 business days).
4. Intake approved -> People Ops opens req in ATS and schedules interview kits and panel assignments.

Intake form example (fields):
| Field | Example / Guidance | Owner | Required? |
| Role title | Senior ML Engineer | Hiring manager | Yes |
| Outcome metrics | Finish X inference pipeline; reduce 95th pct latency to < 150 ms | Hiring manager | Yes |
| Mandatory skills (skill-gate) | GPU inference profiling; TensorRT/ONNX experience; production CI/CD | Hiring manager + team lead | Yes |
| Desired skills | Quantization experience; distributed training knowledge | Hiring manager | No |
| Interview panel | 2 cross-team technical + 1 product + 1 hiring manager | Hiring manager | Yes |
| Start window | 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-15 | Hiring manager | Yes |

2) Skill-gate definition and interview rubric
- Skill-gate must be explicit and testable. Each mandatory skill should have: a one-sentence observable behavior, a pass threshold, and a sample interview question or take-home task.
- Example skill-gate item: "GPU inference profiling" -> Observable: identifies top-3 kernel bottlenecks from a provided profile within 30 minutes and recommends 2 remediation options. Pass threshold: articulated diagnosis + one feasible remediation.
- Interview rubric alignment checklist (to be completed in intake sync):
  - For each panel member: which rubric rows they will own (systems, code quality, product sense, culture fit).
  - Assign scoring scale (0–4) and pass threshold (aggregate >= 12 for senior roles).
  - Confirm take-home vs on-site decision and timeline for grading.

3) Offer and pre-boarding (timeline: 2–5 business days post-offer acceptance)
- Offer approver path: Hiring manager -> People Ops comp reviewer -> Finance sign-off for > 20% over band.
- Pre-boarding packet (sent within 24 hours of offer acceptance): benefits summary, first-day agenda, technical access checklist (VM, corp email, Slack), manager's 2-week plan, mentor assignment, required forms (W-4/Tax, NDA).
- Auto-tasks created in HRIS and onboarding tracker (Workday + internal onboarding tracker).

4) Onboarding sprint (structured 4-week program)
Overview: The goal of the sprint is to establish early wins and objective evidence for the skill-gate. The sprint is a light project-based plan that ends with a manager sign-off against skill-gate evidence artifacts.
Week 0 (Day 0-2): Setup and orientation
- Manager: send welcome note, confirm start-of-day logistics, and share first-week objectives.
- People Ops: ensure equipment shipped, access granted, badge & Slack set up.
- Mentor: 1-hour context walkthrough (systems, stack, key docs).
Deliverables: working dev environment, access to 2 key repos, calendar invites for recurring check-ins.

Week 1: Ramp and observation
- Objectives: Read key docs, run the dev environment, complete a small onboarding task (bugfix or infra sanity check).
- Checkpoint: 30-minute manager sync on Friday with scripted checklist.
Deliverable: PR merged for onboarding task + short writeup of questions and blockers.

Week 2: Guided contribution
- Objectives: Complete a scoped feature or diagnostic relevant to the team (est. 3–8 hours of focused work).
- Mentor pairs for 2 days.
- Checkpoint: End-of-week demo to team (15 minutes).
Deliverable: Demo + PR and test evidence.

Week 3–4: Autonomy & evidence for skill-gate
- Objectives: Independent end-to-end task that exercises the core skill-gate (e.g., profile a model, produce a remediation plan, ship a small perf improvement).
- Checkpoints: 1:1 weekly manager reviews and a mid-sprint mentor review.
- Final deliverable: Skill-gate evidence packet (artifact list below). Manager uses packet to decide role activation.

Skill-gate evidence packet (examples):
- Short writeup (1 page) of the diagnosis and recommended fix.
- PRs with tests and documentation.
- Recorded 10–15 minute demo (screen share) walking through the work.
- Peer feedback from mentor + 2 engineers.

Manager sign-off criteria (role activation):
- Evidence packet meets all mandatory skill-gate items.
- Manager confirms no open critical blockers and that handover to team workflows is complete.
- If unmet, the manager documents a remediation plan (30-day extension with concrete milestones).

5) 30/60/90 and performance signals
- Standard check-in cadence: 1:1 weekly for first 12 weeks, manager-led. Formal calibration at 30, 60, 90 days using the "Onboarding Health Snapshot" template.
- Onboarding Health Snapshot (metrics to capture):
  - Task completion rate (% of assigned onboarding tasks closed on time).
  - Mentor readiness score (1–5).
  - Code quality concerns (yes/no + description).
  - Product impact evidence (demo, customer-impact note).
- Desired target thresholds by day 90: task completion >= 85%, mentor readiness >= 4, no outstanding critical issues.

6) Exceptions and remediation
- Remediation plan: if skill-gate not passed by week 4, create a documented 30-day remediation with measurable milestones and weekly checkpoints. People Ops must be looped within 48 hours of deciding remediation.
- Escalation path: Manager -> People Ops -> Department head -> People Ops leadership if remediation fails after extension.

7) Hiring manager checklist (pre-hire and first 30 days)
Pre-hire: finalize intake, confirm interview rubric, schedule intake sync, nominate mentor, prepare first-week plan.
Day 0–7: complete orientation, verify dev access, run first-week checkpoints.
Day 8–30: execute onboarding sprint tasks, provide continuous feedback, and submit 30-day snapshot to People Ops.

8) Templates and automation
- Intake template: available in Greenhouse integration; fields must be completed before posting req.
- Interview scorecard: standardized Google form (linked in template).
- Onboarding tracker automation: when offer is accepted, Workday triggers a task list for IT and Security (typical tasks: laptop provisioning, VPN access, KMS key request for private deploys if role requires it).
- Sample intake-flow webhook (YAML snippet):
  ---
  req_id: "{{req_id}}"
  title: "Senior Inference Engineer"
  hiring_manager: "alice@example.com"
  skill_gate: ["Profiling", "CUDA kernels", "CI/CD"]
  start_window: "2026-05-01/2026-05-15"
  approvals: ["people-ops", "finance"]

9) Reporting and success metrics (People Ops dashboard)
- Key metrics to track monthly: time from intake -> offer, offer acceptance rate, % hires passing skill-gate at week 4, % hires requiring remediation extension, first-6-month retention.
- Operational SLAs: People Ops responds to intake reviews within 24 hours; intake syncs scheduled within 3 business days.

Appendix: sample 30-day snapshot template (fill-in)
- Name: 
- Role: 
- Manager: 
- Mentor: 
- Tasks assigned / completed: 
- Skill-gate checklist status: [Pass/Partial/Fail] with notes
- Manager recommendation: [Activate / Extend remediation] with reasons

Revision history and governance:
- This doc reviewed quarterly by People Ops and Hiring Committee. Changes to the intake form require approval by Head of People Ops and Head of Recruiting.

Notes and rationale:
We created the skill-gate as a lightweight, evidence-driven checkpoint to reduce ambiguity about early performance and to formalize manager and peer accountability for ramp. The 4-week sprint is intentionally short and focused to produce tangible artifacts that prove readiness or highlight targeted remediation.
